questions.question: Serampore press
questions.solution_html:
• The Serampore Press, also known as the Serampore Mission Press, was a printing press
  • established in Serampore, Danish India, by the British Baptist missionaries William Carey
  • William Ward, and Joshua Marshman in 1800. Initially focused on religious texts, it became a
  • major center for printing in Bengal.
questions.final_answer: major center for printing in Bengal
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how grammar texts and dictionaries helped in the growth of / printing and publishing.
questions.solution_html:
• Grammar text and dictionaries are the basic text used to learn a language. Many missionaries
  • came from foreign nations to India. They forced to learn our languages. So the printing of this
  • text was very necessary. It increased the growth of printing and publishing. Missionaries started
  • educational institutions. It created the need for study materials. Growth of schools enhanced
  • the use of printed books. It flourished printing.
questions.final_answer: the use of printed books. It flourished printing
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how Dr. Hermann Gundert contributed to the growth of printing / and publishing in Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Dr. Hermann Gundert was a famous Basel missionary. The Basel mission centers in India were
  • Thalassery and Mangalapuram. Dr. Hermann Gundert started Rajyasamacharam and
  • Paschimodayam from Illikkunnu in 1847. This is known as the earliest newspapers in Malayalam.
questions.final_answer: Paschimodayam from Illikkunnu in 1847. This is known as the earliest newspapers in Malayalam
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how newspapers united people against colonial oppression.
questions.solution_html:
• Newspapers united people against colonial oppression by acting as a crucial tool for
  • communication, education, and mobilization, thereby fostering a sense of shared identity and
  • purpose across diverse populations.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the role of Mathrubhumi in the freedom struggle.
questions.solution_html:
• Mathrubhoomi played a pivotal role in India's freedom struggle, particularly in Kerala. Founded
  • in 1923 by K.P. Kesava Menon, it served as a powerful mouthpiece for the nationalist
  • movement. Major contributions are: Spreading Nationalist Ideology, Criticizing British Rule
  • Mobilizing Public Opinio, Promoting Social Reforms, Providing a Platform for National Leaders.
questions.final_answer: Mobilizing Public Opinio, Promoting Social Reforms, Providing a Platform for National Leaders
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the significance of Hicky's Bengal Gazette as the first / newspapers in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Hicky's Bengal Gazette was a pioneering English-language newspaper in India, founded by James
  • Augustus Hicky in 1780. Hicky's Bengal Gazette played a significant role in shaping the media
  • landscape in India and influencing the development of journalism in the country.
questions.final_answer: landscape in India and influencing the development of journalism in the country
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write an essay about the importance of Madras in printing.
questions.solution_html:
• Madras is known as the cradle of publishing. Madras played a significant role in the history of
  • printing in India. Madras was one of the earliest locations in India to have a printing press
  • established by the British in the 17th century.
questions.final_answer: established by the British in the 17th century
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the contributions of the press in spreading reform movements / in different regions of India.
questions.solution_html:
• The press played a pivotal role in spreading reform movements across India during the 19th and
  • 20th centuries. Newspapers like Bengal Gazette and Amrita Bazar Patrika promoted social and
  • educational reforms, advocating for women's rights and education. The press highlighted social
  • issues, raising awareness and sparking public debate. The press provided a platform for
  • reformers to express their views, amplifying their message and impact.
questions.final_answer: reformers to express their views, amplifying their message and impact
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write notes on : NBT. (b) CBT. (c ) NCERT
questions.solution_html:
• NBT: National Book Trust functioned as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Human
  • Resource Development. It has had an extensive publishing programme to bring books under
  • different series and make these available to the readers at moderate prices. Books under “India
  • – The Land and the People”, National Biography series, Adan Pradan, Nehru Bala Pustakalaya
  • and Young India Library series etc.
  • CBT: Children’s Book Trust (CBT) is a pioneer publisher of children’s books in India and was
  • founded by cartoonist Shankar in 1957. Children’s Book Trust has set for itself an ambitious
  • target to promote the production of well written, well illustrated and well designed books for
  • children. CBT brought out its first set of illustrated books in 1961.
questions.final_answer: children. CBT brought out its first set of illustrated books in 1961
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
